newsitem.title: PERU: Peru June year-on-year GDP growth 8.2 percent.
newsitem.headline: Peru June year-on-year GDP growth 8.2 percent.

text.p: The Peruvian economy grew 8.2 percent year-on-year in June, compared with 5.1 percent year-on-year growth in the same month last year, the government's statistics agency said Tuesday.
The growth figure was above market expectations. Analysts and brokers consulted by Reuters had predicted a June figure above seven percent.

The National Statistics and Information Institute (INEI) also reported year-on-year Gross Domestic Product growth in the first half was 7.4 percent, compared with 1.8 percent in the same period of 1996.
The June statistic was Peru's second highest year-on-year monthly growth figure so far in 1997. Tops was April's figure of 13.4 percent. May's figure was 6.5 percent.
The government estimates Peru is headed overall year-on-year GDP growth of at least five percent in 1997. GDP rose 2.8 percent in 1996, and 7.0 percent in 1995.

The construction sector also led the way for cumulative year-on-year growth from January to June, with 16.8 percent, followed by agriculture at 8.2 percent, manufacturing at 7.7 percent, commerce at 7.2 percent, "others" at 5.4 percent, mining at 4.8 percent, electricity and water at 4.6 percent, and fishing at 3.2 percent.
